# Intersection of groups generated by convex indivisible-root subsets

`convexRootSubsetGroupIntersection` proves exactly the published proposition
`Langlands.GroupScheme.ConvexRootSubsetGroupIntersectionStatement.{u}`:
for a connected reductive group over an arbitrary field and a maximal split
torus, the supplied groups associated with two individually convex subsets
of the indivisible relative roots intersect in the supplied group associated
with their common roots, on every reduced test scheme.

The proof first handles rational points for full-root closed cone slices
over an algebraically closed field. The actual intersection normalizes the
common-cone group because that group is the identity component of the
intersection. Generated-root-group geometry makes the common-cone group
smooth, affine and connected. The rational-point intersection reduction then
applies maximal-torus conjugacy, normalizer factorization and the convex
Weyl-group intersection theorem.

For the arbitrary base field, the supplied indivisible-root groups have a
smooth scheme-theoretic intersection by their cone semigroup descriptions.
To prove its containment in the common-root group, it therefore suffices to
check points after extension to the algebraic closure. Choose a split maximal
torus containing the extended original torus. Transport each original closed
cone through the split character-lattice equivalence, then pull it back
along restriction from the larger torus. These operations preserve closedness
and intersection. The supplied extended groups are precisely the full-root
groups for the transported cones; no maximality of the extended original
torus is assumed. The algebraically closed rational-point result gives the
needed point containment. Reduced finite-type descent of the smooth
intersection yields containment on all test schemes. In the reverse
direction, the minimality clause of the supplied common-root group puts it
in each of the other groups. The resulting all-test equality implies the
stated reduced-test equivalence.

This is an internal derivation from the Library's root-group generation,
cone semigroup geometry, torus transport, rational normalizer and Weyl
comparisons, and geometric-point factorization theorems. Its implemented
route retains the individual convexity hypotheses throughout and introduces
no new external mathematical premise.
